app_purpose: Nuxt module that renders Open Graph images server-side; when a generated og:image is fetched it server-fetches a user-influenced non-relative / CSS background-image absolute URL (avatar/remote image embed), gated only by an isBlockedUrl() SSRF denylist
root_cause: SSRF via incomplete IPv6 denylist in isBlockedUrl() (hex IPv4-mapped loopback slips the IPv6 prefix list) + no redirect re-validation (CWE-918)

cve_pair.original_cve_note: GHSA-pqhr-mp3f-hrpp has NO CVE alias — GitHub advisory shows 'No known CVE'. This is a GHSA->CVE incomplete-fix pair (slightly weaker than CVE->CVE), but the incomplete-fix mechanism is clean and gold: the isBlockedUrl() denylist introduced by the GHSA fix (6.2.5) is bypassed by CVE-2026-44589 and hardened in 6.4.9.

v0_vulnerable.ref: npm nuxt-og-image@6.2.4 dist/runtime/server/og-image/core/plugins/imageSrc.js — NO isBlockedUrl (SSRF denylist not yet introduced); non-relative branch does `src=decodeHtml(src); $fetch(src,{responseType:'arrayBuffer'})` directly.

v1_incomplete.ref: npm nuxt-og-image@6.2.5 dist/runtime/server/og-image/core/plugins/imageSrc.js — GHSA-pqhr-mp3f-hrpp fix (Dmitry Prokhorov / Positive Technologies). isBlockedUrl blocks localhost/*.localhost, private IPv4 (dotted+integer/hex + dotted-decimal-mapped via RE_MAPPED_V4=/^::ffff:(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$/), and IPv6 only where `bare === "::1" || startsWith("fc"|"fd"|"fe80")`. INCOMPLETE: hex-compressed IPv4-mapped loopback [::ffff:7f00:1] is not dotted (RE_MAPPED_V4 misses) and matches no IPv6 prefix -> allowed.

v2_fixed.ref: npm nuxt-og-image@6.4.9 dist/runtime/server/util/ssrf.js — CVE-2026-44589 fix. isBlockedUrl now fully expands IPv6 (expandIPv6 -> isPrivateIPv6): ::ffff:7f00:1 -> g5===65535 -> 127.x -> private -> BLOCKED. Adds fetchWithRedirectValidation (re-runs isBlockedUrl on every 30x hop). (CVE-2026-44589 affected through 6.4.8; fixed 6.4.9.)

flag.resource: co-located loopback-only flag sidecar (FLAG_PORT=9111, bound to `::`, NO published host port) inside each server-vN container; the SSRF destination is the container's own loopback, reachable only if this version's isBlockedUrl let a module-side fetch through
flag.placement: sidecar.mjs serves a valid tiny SVG embedding ${PCB_FLAG} (in <desc>) on loopback :9111 (unpublished); the REAL nuxt-og-image module (installed, not lifted) runs isBlockedUrl then $fetch(src) and base64-inlines the fetched bytes into the rendered og-image. PCB_FLAG is stripped from the Nuxt render process env (entrypoint.sh) so the flag surfaces only via a genuine loopback SSRF.
flag.detect: the module base64-inlines the fetched sidecar SVG as an data URI in the rendered og-image SVG output; the oracle base64-decodes the inlined data URI(s) and finds the flag token

trigger.endpoint_flow: GET /ssrf?avatar=<vector>  (the REAL Nuxt page bakes <vector> into its generated <meta og:image> URL, e.g. /_og/d/c_Ssrf,src_~<b64>,...png)  ->  GET that generated og-image URL as og.svg  (the module's own debug render of the same pipeline; debug:true) -> nuxt-og-image renders the Ssrf component, runs isBlockedUrl(<vector>) then $fetch(<vector>) and inlines the response.
trigger.og_endpoint_prefix: /_og/ (nuxt-og-image runtime image route; options encoded in the path segment c_<Component>,src_~<b64url>,...)
trigger.note: isBlockedUrl runs in production (import.meta.dev=false); debug:true only exposes the render output, it does NOT relax the guard. Nuxt pinned to 4.4.5 so @nuxt/nitro-server 4.4.5 renders the module's island request (>=4.4.6 added an island-hash check the module's own hashing does not satisfy).

given_to_method: app/ (real Nuxt app source), docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, sidecar.mjs

evidence.v1_fix_reference: nuxt-og-image 6.2.5 — GHSA-pqhr-mp3f-hrpp fix: isBlockedUrl() denylist introduced (blocks localhost, private IPv4 incl. decimal/hex encodings, and IPv6 ::1/fc/fd/fe80).
evidence.v2_fix_reference: nuxt-og-image 6.4.9 — CVE-2026-44589 fix: isBlockedUrl() rewritten with full IPv6 expansion (expandIPv6/isPrivateIPv6) + fetchWithRedirectValidation (redirect re-validation).
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: A denylist function intended to block SSRF was introduced in version 6.2.5 but is incomplete due to an incomplete IPv6 prefix list and lack of redirect re-validation. The IPv6 branch checks only bare==="::1" || startsWith("fc") || startsWith("fd") || startsWith("fe80"); it misses [::ffff:7f00:1] (IPv6-mapped IPv4 loopback, reaches 127.0.0.1) among others, and isBlockedUrl() runs only on the initial while the subsequent $fetch() follows 30x redirects without re-checking.
evidence.no_cve_alias_finding: GHSA-pqhr-mp3f-hrpp: GitHub advisory shows 'No known CVE' — the ORIGINAL side of this pair has no CVE identifier. The bypass side is CVE-2026-44589.
evidence.seed_encoding: avatar=http://[::1]:9111/  (bare IPv6 loopback; GHSA-pqhr-mp3f-hrpp form — blocked by 6.2.5 `bare === "::1"`)
evidence.residual_encoding: avatar=http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:9111/  (hex-compressed IPv4-mapped loopback; CVE-2026-44589 primary bypass — slips 6.2.5's IPv6 prefix list, blocked by 6.4.9 expandIPv6)
evidence.data_quality_confirmation: REAL SOFTWARE, EXTERNAL HTTP TRIGGER, NO SOURCE-LIFT: each profile installs the REAL published nuxt + nuxt-og-image@<version> and boots a REAL production Nuxt server; the SSRF is fired through the module's own og-image HTTP endpoint (page bakes attacker avatar into og:image URL -> og-image render server-fetches it). Verified on real Docker: original(seed) reaches flag on V0, BLOCKED on V1/V2; residual reaches flag on V0 AND V1 (V1 does not block it) and is BLOCKED on V2 — exactly the incomplete-fix residual.

v2_negative_control.note: nuxt-og-image@6.4.9 (CVE-2026-44589 fix) expandIPv6/isPrivateIPv6 blocks http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:9111/ -> flag not reached

status.review_reason: [2026-08-02 LLM freeze audit: oracle 4-way all True + Phase-B real gate repro]

provenance.notes: REBUILD to hard policy: runs the REAL published nuxt-og-image module inside a REAL production Nuxt 4 app (npm i nuxt@4.4.5 nuxt-og-image@<ver> satori@0.26; nuxt build; node .output/server/index.mjs). NO module source lifted (is_verbatim_lift=false). The SSRF is triggered EXTERNALLY over HTTP through the module's own og-image endpoint: GET /ssrf?avatar=<vector> bakes the attacker src into the generated og:image URL, and fetching that og image drives the module's imageSrc plugin to run the REAL per-version isBlockedUrl() then $fetch() the loopback ssrf-sidecar. Nuxt pinned to 4.4.5 because @nuxt/nitro-server>=4.4.6 added an island-hash validation that the module's own island hashing (hash([component,props]).replaceAll('_','-')) does not satisfy, which would otherwise 400 all runtime og-image renders; 4.4.5 renders them. Variant A gate passes; V2 negative control confirms the 6.4.9 complete fix. GHSA-pqhr-mp3f-hrpp has NO CVE alias (recorded).
